app.name: Telegram Messenger
app.description: Pure instant messaging — simple, fast, secure, and synced across all your devices. One of the top 5 most downloaded apps in the world with over 1 billion active users.

verdict.one_liner: A privacy-focused messaging app that doesn't show ads, but uploads your contacts to its servers.
verdict.summary: Telegram Messenger is a popular cloud-based messaging service with a strong commitment to privacy. Unlike most competitors, Telegram explicitly promises not to use your data for advertising. It offers end-to-end encrypted Secret Chats and stores regular messages encrypted in the cloud. However, the app uploads your contacts to its servers and shares some data with third parties for optional features like translation.
verdict.recommendation_reason: Excellent privacy stance on advertising combined with strong encryption options. The contact syncing is the main concern, but it's optional and deletable.

red.title: Your contacts are uploaded to Telegram's servers
red.plain_english: When you sync contacts, Telegram stores your contacts' names and phone numbers on its servers to notify you when they join. While you can delete this data anytime, it happens without your contacts' explicit consent.

red.title: Phone number is your unique identifier
red.plain_english: Telegram uses your phone number as your account identifier. While you can set a username to hide your number, your phone number is visible to anyone who has it in their contacts.

red.title: Messages sent to Google for translation
red.plain_english: When you use the translate feature, your message text is sent to Google or Microsoft for translation. These companies promise not to use the data for other purposes.

red.title: Voice messages sent to Google for transcription
red.plain_english: When Premium users convert voice messages to text, the audio is sent to Google for transcription. Google promises not to log or use the data for other purposes.

green.title: Telegram promises not to use your data for ads
green.plain_english: Telegram has a fundamental principle: 'We don't use your data to show you ads.' This is rare for a free app and is a significant privacy advantage.

green.title: Secret Chats use end-to-end encryption
green.plain_english: Secret Chats use end-to-end encryption, meaning only you and the recipient can read messages. Telegram cannot decrypt them, and they are not stored on servers.

green.title: Open source with verifiable builds
green.plain_english: Telegram's apps are open source, and they provide reproducible builds so you can verify the app you download matches the published source code.

green.title: Inactive accounts automatically delete
green.plain_english: If you don't use Telegram for 18 months (configurable), your account and all data are automatically deleted. You can also manually delete your account anytime.

green.title: Delete messages for both sides anytime
green.plain_english: In one-on-one chats, either party can delete any message for both participants with no time limit. This gives you control over your conversation history.

categories.label: Camera & Microphone
categories.plain_english: Camera and microphone are used on-demand for video calls, voice messages, and sending photos. They're not required for basic messaging.
categories.detail: Camera and microphone access is optional and user-initiated. Used for video calls, voice messages, and capturing photos/videos to send.
categories.policy_excerpt: Telegram uses standard device permissions for camera and microphone when you initiate calls or record media.
concerns: No specific concerns about camera/mic usage

categories.label: Location & GPS
categories.plain_english: Location is only collected when you choose to share it, like sending your location in a chat or using Live Location. Live Location works in the background while active.
categories.detail: Location data is treated like messages and only collected when you actively share it. Live Location and 'People Nearby' features can access location in background while enabled.
categories.policy_excerpt: If you share your Live Location in any chat or turn on 'Make Myself Visible' in People Nearby, Telegram will use your data to display your location to those users with whom you are sharing it, even when the app is closed – for as long as you keep these optional features activated.
concerns: Live Location works in background while active
Location shared with other users when you choose to share it

categories.label: Contacts & Phonebook
categories.plain_english: Telegram asks before syncing your contacts. If you agree, your contacts' names and phone numbers are stored on Telegram's servers to notify you when they join. You can delete this data anytime.
categories.detail: Contact syncing is optional but recommended for the service to work well. Telegram stores only the name and phone number of contacts, nothing else. Users can stop syncing or delete contacts from servers in Settings. The data is not sold or shared with advertisers.
categories.policy_excerpt: We store your up-to-date contacts in order to notify you as soon as one of your contacts signs up for Telegram and to properly display names in notifications. We only need the number and name (first and last) for this to work and store no other data about your contacts.
concerns: Contacts uploaded to external servers without contacts' consent
Phone number used as unique identifier

categories.label: Storage & File Access
categories.plain_english: Files you send are stored encrypted on Telegram's servers so you can access them from any device. Secret chat files are encrypted with keys Telegram doesn't have.
categories.detail: Files sent in cloud chats are stored encrypted on servers. Files in secret chats are encrypted before upload with keys only the sender and recipient have. Media is periodically purged from servers.
categories.policy_excerpt: When you send photos, videos or files via secret chats, before being uploaded, each item is encrypted with a separate key, not known to the server.
concerns: Cloud chat media stored on servers
Regular chats don't have end-to-end encryption by default

categories.label: Data Sharing with 3rd Parties
categories.plain_english: Telegram shares minimal data: with group companies (for operations), law enforcement (with valid legal orders), and optional service providers (Google/Microsoft for translation/transcription). They explicitly do not sell data.
categories.detail: Data is shared with: group companies (Telegram Group Inc, Telegraph Inc, Telegram FZ-LLC), law enforcement with valid judicial orders, Google/Microsoft for translation when user requests it, and Google for transcription when Premium users request it. Payment data goes to third-party payment providers.
categories.policy_excerpt: Neither Telegram nor the merchants on the platform (bot developers) have access to this information. Although we work with payment providers they are completely independent from Telegram.
concerns: Data shared with Google for translation and transcription
Data shared with group companies in different jurisdictions
IP and phone number may be disclosed to law enforcement

categories.label: Account & Identity Data
categories.plain_english: You need a phone number to sign up. Your screen name, username, and profile picture are public. Optional info includes birthday and email for recovery.
categories.detail: Phone number is required for account creation. Screen name, username (if set), and profile pictures are always public. Optional data includes birthday, business location, and email for 2FA recovery.
categories.policy_excerpt: You provide your mobile number and basic account data (which may include profile name, profile picture and about information) to create a Telegram account. The screen name you choose, your profile pictures, and your username (should you choose to set one) on Telegram are always public.
concerns: Phone number required for signup
Profile information is public by default

categories.label: Behavioural & Ad Tracking
categories.plain_english: Telegram explicitly promises they do NOT use your data for ads. They only show sponsored messages in public channels based on the channel topic, not your personal data.
categories.detail: Telegram has a fundamental principle of not using user data for advertising. Sponsored messages in public channels are based solely on channel topic, not user profiling. No ad targeting based on personal data.
categories.policy_excerpt: We don't use your data to show you ads. Telegram only stores the information it needs to function as a secure and feature-rich cloud service. No user data is mined or analyzed to display ads or sponsored messages.

categories.label: Children's Data Handling
categories.plain_english: The app is rated 12+ but the policy doesn't specifically address children's data protections. Telegram does not appear to be designed for children under 13.
categories.detail: App Store rating is 12+. Policy mentions using age data to determine eligibility for age-specific content. No specific COPPA or GDPR-K compliance language found.
categories.policy_excerpt: We may use data about your age to determine your eligibility for accessing age-specific content.
concerns: No explicit children's data protection policy
App rated 12+ but phone number required

categories.label: Network & Internet Activity
categories.plain_english: Telegram collects metadata like your IP address and device information for security and spam prevention. This data is kept for a maximum of 12 months.
categories.detail: IP addresses, device info, and app usage metadata are collected for security, spam prevention, and fraud detection. Metadata can be kept for up to 12 months maximum.
categories.policy_excerpt: To improve the security of your account, as well as to prevent spam, abuse, and other violations of our Terms of Service, we may collect metadata such as your IP address, devices and Telegram apps you've used, history of username changes, etc. If collected, this metadata can be kept for 12 months maximum.
concerns: IP addresses collected and stored up to 12 months
Device information logged for security

categories.label: Device Info & Fingerprinting
categories.plain_english: Telegram collects device information and app metadata for security purposes, like preventing spam and unauthorized access. This data is stored for up to 12 months.
categories.detail: Device information and Telegram apps used are collected as part of security metadata. Used for spam prevention, fraud detection, and account security. Stored up to 12 months.
categories.policy_excerpt: We may collect metadata such as your IP address, devices and Telegram apps you've used, history of username changes, etc.
concerns: Device info logged for security
Used for spam prevention and fraud detection

categories.label: Health & Biometric Data
categories.plain_english: Telegram does not collect health or biometric data. Face ID or fingerprint unlock is handled locally by your device.
categories.detail: No health or biometric data collection mentioned in policy. Biometric authentication (Face ID, fingerprint) would be handled by device's native security, not by Telegram.

categories.label: Financial & Payment Data
categories.plain_english: Payment information is handled by third-party providers. Telegram never sees or stores your credit card details. They can store shipping info if you choose to save it.
categories.detail: Credit card info goes directly to payment providers, never touches Telegram servers. Telegram receives a token for future payments. Shipping info can be stored if user chooses. Users can clear payment data anytime in settings.
categories.policy_excerpt: When making a purchase, you enter your credit card details into a form supplied by the payment provider that will be processing the payment, and this information goes directly to the payment provider's server. Your credit card information never reaches Telegram's servers.
concerns: Shipping information may be stored
Payment data shared with third-party providers

categories.label: Data Deletion & User Rights
categories.plain_english: You have strong rights: you can delete your account which removes all data, export your data, delete synced contacts, and delete messages for both sides. Inactive accounts auto-delete after 18 months.
categories.detail: Account deletion removes all messages, media, contacts, and data from Telegram cloud. Users can request data export. GDPR rights supported with EEA representative. Self-destruct timer for inactive accounts (default 18 months, configurable). Messages can be deleted for both sides in 1-on-1 chats.
categories.policy_excerpt: Deleting your account removes all messages, media, contacts and every other piece of data you store in the Telegram cloud. You have rights to: request a copy of all your personal data, delete or amend your personal data, restrict or object to processing, correct inaccurate data, and lodge complaints with data protection authorities.
concerns: Cloud chat messages remain until recipient also deletes them

categories.label: Policy Change Notification
categories.plain_english: Policy changes are posted on the website. Important changes are notified via Telegram. Continued use after changes equals acceptance.
categories.detail: Changes effective immediately when posted. Important changes are notified via Telegram. Users are asked to check the website frequently for updates. A changelog of significant updates is maintained.
categories.policy_excerpt: Any changes to this Privacy Policy will become effective when we post the revised Privacy Policy on this page www.telegram.org/privacy. Important changes made to this Privacy Policy will be notified to you via Telegram.
concerns: Changes effective immediately upon posting
No specific advance notice period mentioned
